## Incident Report: STRRAT RAT Infection — 2024-07-30

### Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.16.1.66 | Source of all suspicious traffic; local /24 (172.16.1.0/24), gateway 172.16.1.1 |
| MAC | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 | ARP records binding 172.16.1.66 to this MAC (frames with arp.opcode 1/2) |
| Hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F | NBNS Workstation/Server registrations from 172.16.1.66; Kerberos `CNameString` = `desktop-skbr25f$`; also self-reported inside the malware's own C2 beacon |
| Logged-in user | ccollier | Kerberos `CNameString` = `ccollier` (TGS-REQ/REP with the domain controller 172.16.1.4); also self-reported inside the malware's own C2 beacon |

Domain controller for context: 172.16.1.4 (`WIRESHARK-WS-DC.wiresharkworkshop.online`, MAC 5c:f9:dd:8c:97:35), domain `wiresharkworkshop.online`.

### Malware Family
**STRRAT** (Java-based RAT/credential stealer). **Attribution: signature-confirmed** — not by an IDS signature file (none was provided in the evidence set), but by the malware's own C2 check-in protocol, which prints its family name in plaintext on every beacon (see below). This is direct first-party evidence, not a behavioral guess.

### C2 Traffic (grounded evidence)
TCP stream 83 (`tcp.stream==83`), 172.16.1.66:49754 → 141.98.10.79:12132, opened at capture-relative time 76.99s and beaconing continuously every ~5 seconds through the end of the capture (585.66s). No DNS lookup preceded this connection — the C2 IP:port is hardcoded, contacted directly. Follow-TCP-ASCII of the stream shows a repeating cleartext pipe-delimited check-in:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender||1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|1 Sec
```

Fields decode to: protocol verb `ping`, malware family `STRRAT`, campaign/bot ID `1BE8292C`, victim hostname, victim user, OS, architecture, installed AV (Windows Defender), STRRAT version `1.6`, geolocation `US:United States`, and an uptime counter. Later beacons add a base64 field `UHJvZ3JhbSBNYW5hZ2Vy` which decodes to `Program Manager` (active desktop window title).

Immediately before the C2 connection (frame 9111, t=78.01s), the host made a plaintext HTTP GET to `ip-api.com/json/` (resolved to 208.95.112.1) with a spoofed Chrome user-agent — consistent with STRRAT's known victim-geolocation step feeding the `US:United States` field seen in the beacon. `ip-api.com` is a legitimate public API abused here, not inherently malicious infrastructure, so it is listed as context rather than a hard IOC.

### Delivery Chain (partial — traffic is encrypted)
In the ~13 seconds before the first C2 beacon, the host resolved and connected via TLS to `github.com` (140.82.113.3), `objects.githubusercontent.com` (185.199.110.133, ~833 KB transferred), and `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209, ~8.87 MB transferred), all between t=64s and t=74s — immediately followed by STRRAT's first C2 beacon at t=78s. This timing is consistent with STRRAT's documented behavior of pulling its loader/dependency jars from GitHub release assets and legitimate Maven Central artifacts at first run. However, this traffic is TLS-encrypted; no plaintext URL, filename, or file content was recoverable from the capture, so **no file name or SHA256 hash can be grounded in this evidence**. These three domains/IPs are legitimate CDN/repository infrastructure and are listed as benign context, not confirmed-malicious IOCs — the correlation is behavioral, not proven.

### IOC Summary (JSON)

    "ip": "172.16.1.66",
    "mac": "00:1e:64:ec:f3:08",
    "hostname": "DESKTOP-SKBR25F",
    "user": "ccollier"
  },
  "malware_family": "STRRAT",
  "attribution_confidence": "signature-confirmed",
  "iocs": [
    {
      "type": "c2_endpoint",
      "value": "141.98.10.79:12132",
      "evidence": "tcp.stream==83, 172.16.1.66:49754 <-> 141.98.10.79:12132, continuous 5-second beacons from t=76.99s to end of capture (585.66s); cleartext payload 'ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|...' recovered via tshark follow,tcp,ascii"
    }
  ],
  "benign_context": [
    {"note": "ip-api.com (208.95.112.1) — legitimate geolocation API, HTTP GET /json/ at frame 9111, spoofed Chrome UA; timing/content correlates with the 'US:United States' field in the STRRAT beacon but the service itself is not malicious infrastructure"},
    {"note": "github.com (140.82.113.3), objects.githubusercontent.com (185.199.110.133), repo1.maven.org (199.232.196.209) — legitimate CDN/repository infrastructure; TLS-encrypted downloads occurring t=64-74s, immediately before first C2 beacon; plausible but unconfirmed delivery/dependency-fetch vector, content not recoverable from ciphertext"},
    {"note": "All LDAP, Kerberos, DCE/RPC, SMB2, NBNS, mDNS, LLMNR, SSDP, CLDAP traffic between 172.16.1.66 and 172.16.1.4 (WIRESHARK-WS-DC) — normal Active Directory domain member behavior (GPO pull of GptTmpl.inf/Registry.pol, SAMR, DFS referrals)"},
    {"note": "Microsoft telemetry/services traffic (assets.msn.com, client.wns.windows.com, login.microsoftonline.com, officeapps.live.com, bing.com, skype, oracle javadl, wpad.wiresharkworkshop.online, etc.) — standard Windows 11 / Office background noise"}
  ],
  "incident_summary": "Windows 11 workstation DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as user ccollier, is infected with the STRRAT RAT (bot ID 1BE8292C, malware-reported version 1.6). Starting at capture time 78s the host establishes continuous 5-second cleartext beaconing to a hardcoded C2 at 141.98.10.79:12132, self-identifying as STRRAT in every check-in and reporting host OS, AV product, and active window title. The infection is preceded by a victim-geolocation query to ip-api.com and encrypted downloads from GitHub and Maven Central, consistent with but not proof of STRRAT's known delivery/dependency-fetch pattern; no file name or hash could be recovered because that traffic is TLS-encrypted."
